added_lines: reflection for the solemnity of all saints today, the church celebrates the solemnity of all saints - not only the famous saints we know by name, but also the countless men and women from every nation, language, and race who lived quiet, faithful lives and now enjoy the presence of god. think of our great-grandparents who may have lived very good lives but were not canonised as saints by the church. the vision in the book of revelation in our first reading (apocalypse 7: 2-4,9-14) reminds us that heaven is not empty; it is filled with a great multitude who have washed their robes in the blood of the lamb. in other words, holiness is not a dream reserved for a few special people. it is the calling of every christian. the second reading from (1 john 3:1-3) tells us something even more beautiful: “ we are already children of god .” this means holiness begins now. it is not something we wait for until after death. it starts in our daily choices, in the way we speak, forgive, work, pray, and relate with others. to be a saint is simply to belong to god and to allow his grace to shape our lives. do you want to be a saint? don't wait till tomorrow, begin today to do good and strive towards holiness of life. the gospel (matthew 5:1-12) on the beatitudes gives us the path to attain this holiness. jesus says that the poor in spirit, the gentle, the merciful, the pure in heart, the peacemakers, and those who hunger for justice are blessed. these are not just beautiful words; they are practical lessons for daily life. holiness i s lived when we choose honesty over lies, humility over pride, forgiveness over revenge, prayer over despair, and peace over conflict. the saints teach us that holiness is possible in ordinary life. it is possible in the home, in the workplace, in the classroom, in illness, in old age, and even in suffering. the saints were not perfect people; they were people who kept returning to god. they failed, repented, trusted, and persevered. today, let us ask for the grace to live like the saints: to be faithful in sm all things, generous in love, patient in trials, and hopeful in god’s promises. may this feast renew our desire for heaven and remind us that the road to glory is walked one day, one decision, and one act of love at a time. all saints, pray for us. longford (templemichael)

. as always, you book your own entry ticket to the show. come along to the hill on tuesday 3rd november to meet our group. lotto draw held on monday 26th october 2026. no's drawn: 02-05-16-17. no jackpot winner. draw winners: €30 €5 envelopes to paddy killian, €30 to paul rowley, €20 each to james flynn and chris cox. next weeks draw will be held in the local on monday 2nd november and the jackpot is €4,800. lotto team on next week's draw is ronan muldoon, ray moynihan and paddy killian. thanks for your support. reasons why we honour the saints: 1- the saints lived heroic lives of faith. st. paul asks us to serve and honour such noble souls. he advises christians to welcome, serve, and honour those who have put their trust in jesus. the saints enjoy heavenly bliss as a reward for their faith in jesus. hence, they deserve our veneration. 2- the saints are our role models. they teach us by their lives that christ's holy life of love, mercy and forgiveness can, with the grace of god, be lived by ordinary people from all walks of life and at all times. 3- the saints are our heavenly mediators who intercede for us before jesus, the only mediator between god and us. 4- the saints are the instruments that god uses to work miracles in the present. on the feast of all saints, the church invites and challenges us to walk the walk of the saints, not just talk the talk: "not everyone who says to me, 'lord, lord,' will enter the kingdom of heaven, but only the one who does the will of my father in heaven" (mt 7:21). 2) the feast gives us an occasion to thank god for having invited so many of our ancestors to join the company of the saints. may our reflection on the heroic lives of the saints, with our imitation of their lifestyle, enable us to hear from our lord the words of grand welcome to eternal bliss: "well done, good and faithful servant! enter into the joys of your master" (mt 25:21). we need to pray to the saints, both the canonized and the uncanonized, asking them to pray on our behalf that we may live our lives in faithfulness like theirs, and so receive the same reward they are enjoying. november intentions: those who wish to have their deceased remembered in masses during november, please fill in the form available at each entrance & drop into the box provided in front of the altar.
norms for indulgences at the commemoration of all souls

from 12 noon on nov 1st to midnight on nov 2nd, all who have confessed, received holy communion and prayed for the pope's intentions (one our father & one hail mary, can gain one plenary indulgence by visiting a church, and there reciting one our father & the apostle's creed. this indulgence is applicable only to the souls of the departed. confession may be made any time within the week preceding or the week following nov 1. the faithful who visit a cemetery and pray for the dead may gain a plenary indulgence applicable only to the holy souls by saying the above prayers once per day from nov 1st to 8th.
